_comment: Module 6 — MVP coding-problem catalog. A small, high-quality set covering arrays/strings/hash maps/binary search/stacks-queues/trees/graphs/dynamic programming (module §8), not hundreds of generated ones. Every problem is stdin/stdout based (the sandbox runs a whole program, not a function call) — starter_code is I/O scaffolding only, never a working solution. app/services/coding/catalog_seed.py only reads this file; adding a problem is a data change, never a code change.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers and a target value, return the 0-indexed positions of the two numbers that add up to target, in increasing order, separated by a space. Exactly one valid answer exists.

Input:
  n
  a_1 a_2 ... a_n
  target
Output:
  i j   (0-indexed, i < j)

starter_code.python:
n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
target = int(input())
# TODO: find the two indices whose values sum to target

problems.title: Maximum Level Sum in a Binary Tree
problems.description:
A binary tree is given as an explicit node array: each node has a value and the indices of its left/right children (-1 if none). Find the maximum sum of node values across any single level (root is level 1).

Input:
  n
  val_0 left_0 right_0
  ...
  val_{n-1} left_{n-1} right_{n-1}
  root_index
Output:
  the maximum level sum

nodes = [tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
